# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## Local Chrome

The default daemon can keep many tabs and visit many sites; browser-use has
no per-site, screenshot, or result-count limit that requires a new daemon.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

While bypass permissions mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools.      1	---
     2	name: brain-audit-loop
     3	description: "The /brain-audit skill — what it scores, where reports and the trend live, and the manual-vs-cron failure it exists to catch"
     4	metadata: 
     5	  node_type: memory
     6	  type: project
     7	  originSessionId: 83464d9d-8262-4ca8-9aed-13167ae4fa1f
     8	  modified: 2026-09-08T02:32:14.657Z

    10	
    11	Built 2026-09-07 from a gap analysis of a Nate Herk AIOS video. The video's own
    12	content was mostly things already built better here (routing map, graphify,
    13	command centre); the four things missing were a **recurring scored audit**, a
    14	**level-up step**, a **topic-driven grill that files itself**, and a **rubric for
    15	"is this working"**. Analysis: `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-07-aios-video-gap-analysis.md`.
    16	
    17	**The skill:** `~/.claude/skills/brain-audit/` — `SKILL.md` plus `measure.sh`
    18	(deterministic facts, ~7s). Scores the four C's (context, connections,
    19	capabilities, cadence) 25 points each, runs three pass/fail tests, writes
    20	`~/SecondBrain/audits/brain-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, appends one row to
    21	`~/SecondBrain/audits/_trend.md`, and proposes **exactly two** builds. Paths are
    22	registered in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.json` as `vault_audits` /
    23	`vault_audit_trend`.
    24	
    25	**Baseline 2026-09-07: 67/100** (context 17, connections 22, capabilities 15,
    26	cadence 13). Two builds it proposed and Eric has not yet started: `/grill-me
    27	<topic>` writing to `Inbox/grills/`, and putting `/brain-audit` on the monthly
    28	`com.keystone.rituals` timer.
    29	
    30	**Why:** The recurring failure in this system is not bloat or drift — it is that
    31	**everything with a cron stays alive and everything manual freezes inside six
    32	weeks.** Measured twice: `Notes/` froze 2026-06-05, restarted after the
    33	2026-07-24 audit (11 → 23 notes), froze again 2026-08-03. The single prior audit
    34	sat alone for 45 days. A scored trend is the countermeasure, and it only works if
    35	it is itself on a timer.
    36	
    37	**How to apply:** Don't score `Inbox/` freshness as health — it is cron-fed by
    38	`meeting-sync` and grows daily regardless. `Notes/` and `Drafts/` are the honest
    39	signal, which is why cadence is scored on `Notes/` rather than on job exit codes.
    40	When proposing builds, prefer automating an existing manual step over adding a new
    41	capability, and check the proposal against [[user_working-conditions-bottleneck]] —
    42	the grill-me build was chosen because that memory says the limiting factor is the
    43	absence of a thinking partner and the right move is helping him capture what
    44	surfaces. Stay off two neighbours' territory: `claude-stack-doctor` owns plumbing,
    45	`improve-system` owns note-level rot. Related: [[project_keystoneos-verification-habits]],
    46	[[feedback_ingest-review-gate]].

    15	> shutdown — then run `/backup`. Leave CRASHBOX attached at 21:00 or the SSD layer skips.

    18	> 0xC000013A is the sleep-kill signature, see [[backup-task-sleepkill-signature]]), and

    20	> stays disabled — the script is the macOS port.

    22	**Current state (2026-09-03).** Two backup runs happen on most days, and the 09-02 entry was
    23	right about that — but **not** because reconcile hard-codes the backup. The real mechanism,
    24	traced 09-03:
    25	
    26	`keystone-reconcile.ps1` is a **generic make-up engine**. It has no mention of `daily-backup` at
    27	all; it loops the registry at `DEV/KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` and calls
    28	`run-job.ps1 -Job <id> -Trigger reconcile -MadeUp` for any job with no success recorded today.
    29	The `daily-backup` job is in that registry with `reconcile: true`, `graceMinutes: 60`,
    30	`maxAttemptsPerDay: 2`, and `makeupWindow: 07:00-20:00`. Its `successProbe` greps today's
    31	`daily-backup.log` for `daily-backup end: OK`. So:
    32	
    33	- **If no successful run is recorded by 07:00, reconcile replays it** → the ~07:00-07:10 run.
    34	- **launchd `com.keystone.dailybackup` fires at 09:00 regardless** → the second run.
    35	- **Run the backup by hand before 07:00 and reconcile skips it** ("already succeeded today").
    36	  Confirmed 09-03: a 06:15 manual run logged `OK` at 06:25, and no 07:00 run happened.

    39	plist fires at 09:00. The make-up window is what actually drives the 07:00 replay, so the stale
    40	`at` has not bitten yet. Still true: `launchctl ... runs = 0` proves nothing — read the log.

    45	no `PUSH FAILED`, no `PUSH ERR`. But the **reconcile/`run-job.ps1`** context — which is where the
...

{"id":"daily-backup","label":"Daily memory + repo backup","taskName":"KeystoneOS-DailyBackup","exe":"pwsh","script":"{USERPROFILE}/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1","schedule":{"kind":"daily","at":"12:00"},"graceMinutes":60,"timeoutMinutes":240,"maxAttemptsPerDay":2,"reconcile":true,"makeupWindow":{"from":"12:00","to":"20:00"},"successProbe":{"kind":"fileContains","path":"{USERPROFILE}/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log","pattern":"^{DATE} .*daily-backup end: OK"}}

#!/bin/bash
# Gate for daily-backup.ps1. Both launchd jobs call it:
#   com.keystone.dailybackup        hourly 12:00-17:00, so a failed try gets another chance
#   com.keystone.dailybackup-login  at login, so a Mac that was off still gets a backup
# Runs the backup only when: no run ended OK today, the Mac is on AC power, no backup is
# running, and fewer than 2 real runs started today (a lasting error must not run 6 times).
# Why daytime + AC: every 21:00 run from 10-13 to 10-22 ended ERROR because the Mac slept
# on battery, and caffeinate -s only holds sleep off on AC (audit 2026-10-22).
# shortcut: checks the log, not a lock file; two runs at the same moment could both start.
LOG="${BACKUP_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log}"
TODAY=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
skip() { echo "$(date '+%F %T') gate skip: $1"; exit 0; }

grep -q "^$TODAY .*daily-backup end: OK" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null && skip "already OK today"
pmset -g ps | grep -q "AC Power" || skip "on battery"
# [.] keeps the pattern from matching any shell whose command line merely mentions the script
pgrep -f "pwsh.*daily-backup[.]ps1" >/dev/null && skip "a backup is already running"
STARTS=$(grep -c "^$TODAY .*daily-backup start (DryRun=False)" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)
[ "${STARTS:-0}" -ge 2 ] && skip "2 tries already today"

exec /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1"

content.content:
Fireflies CLI — Every Fireflies meeting feature, plus offline search, cross-meeting intelligence, and a local database no other tool ha…

Highlights (not in the official API docs):
  • transcripts search   Full-text search across all synced meeting transcripts without consuming any API quota.
  • person timeline   Chronological meeting history with a specific person — topics, action items, and talk ratio per meeting.
  • action-items list   Aggregate action items from all meetings in a date range — weekly commitment audit in one command.
  • transcripts find   Find meetings by participant email, channel name, keyword, or date range — all client-side, no broken API date filters.
  • transcripts status   Show PROCESSED / PROCESSING / FAILED status for recent meetings upfront — know before you fetch.
  • topics list   Most frequent topics across all meetings in a date range — what is actually consuming meeting time.
  • digest   Aggregate view of all recent meetings: titles, gists, topics, and action items in one structured output.
  • transcripts export   Export a transcript as markdown to a vault directory with auto-generated YYYY-MM-DD_title.md filename.

Agent mode: add --agent to any command for JSON output + non-interactive mode.
Health check: run 'fireflies-pp-cli doctor' to verify auth and connectivity.
See README.md or the bundled SKILL.md for recipes.

Usage:
  fireflies-pp-cli [command]

Available Commands:
  action-items  Extract action items from transcripts
  agent-context Emit structured JSON describing this CLI for agents
  analytics     Query meeting analytics
  api           Browse all API endpoints by interface name
  auth          Manage authentication for Fireflies
  channels      Get a single channel
  completion    Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  digest        Aggregate summary of recent meetings — titles, decisions, and action items
  doctor        Check CLI health
  feedback      Record feedback about this CLI (local by default; upstream opt-in)
  help          Help about any command
  import        Import data from JSONL file via API create/upsert calls
  keywords      Get AI-extracted keywords for a transcript
  person        Person-centric views across all meetings
  profile       Named sets of flags saved for reuse
  speakers      Show per-speaker analytics for a transcript
  summary       Get the AI-generated summary for a transcript
  sync          Sync Fireflies transcripts to local SQLite for offline search and analysis

25	reflection is expensive when tired and this ritual already lapsed 49 days once. The
26	"N of D" count is the nudge; never backfill missing days to make it look better. Never

28	editing, so an invented install becomes a false claim in front of Chris Ruf.
